samples.summary: Notification-planning rule re-implemented in the backend instead of shared with the frontend's `planCommentNotifications` — two implementations that already give different answers
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:50` already owns this exact rule (`planCommentNotifications`), together with `toUserId` (notify.ts:29), `uniqueUserIds` (notify.ts:139) and mention extraction via `extractMentionedUserIds` / `MENTION_RE` (`packages/frontend/src/components/comments/mentions.ts:24,136`). The diff restates all four in `comments.controller.ts` (`planCommentNotifications` L532, `toUserId` L513, `participantIds` L590, `MENTION_RE` L504) with a docblock that explicitly says it "mirrors" them. The repo's stated expectation is reuse of shared logic (`@wafflebase/core`, or `@wafflebase/sheets`' `comment/` module which the backend already depends on and which already owns `Thread`/`createThread`/`deleteComment`). The two copies have already diverged on user-visible output: the frontend passes `preview(comment.body)` = `mentionBodyToPlainText(body).slice(0, 200)` (notify.ts:35-37,92), while the backend passes the raw body (`preview: comment.body`, L568), so a mention notification opened by an agent-authored comment shows the raw `@[name](9)` markup where a browser-authored one shows `@name`. verdict.reason: All four claimed re-implementations are present in the backend controller exactly as described: MENTION_RE (comments.controller.ts:504), toUserId (:511, identical body to notify.ts:29-33), planCommentNotifications (:532) and participantIds (:596), with docblocks at :89 and :520 stating outright that the rule is the frontend's planCommentNotifications restated. The frontend originals are at notify.ts:50/29/139 with mention extraction in mentions.ts:24,136. The reply/mention dedupe rule is duplicated verbatim (controller :580 vs notify.ts:99). The claimed divergence is real and user-visible: the frontend sends mentionBodyToPlainText(body).slice(0,200) (notify.ts:35-37, used at :73,92,108), rendering mentions as @username (mentions.ts:124-130), while the backend sends the raw body (:550,:572,:588). The server-side sanitizePreview (notification.service.ts:67-82, applied at :150) only removes invisible/control chars, collapses whitespace and truncates — it does not normalize @[name](id) markup, so it does not close the gap. Reuse was structurally available: this same controller already imports @wafflebase/sheets (:41-46) and that package has a comment module (packages/sheets/src/comment/thread.ts, types.ts, anchor.ts). The duplicated code is on all live write paths (:290,:320,:351,:383), so nothing guards it away. Duplication/reuse is explicitly in this lens's lane and the rubric grades already-diverged duplicate logic as major.

finding.summary: Comment/thread delete routes enforce no author check, contradicting the documented "delete by author only" lifecycle
finding.evidence: `deleteThread` and `deleteComment` take only `@Param`s — no `@Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest` and no comparison of `req.user.id` against `comment.author.userId` — so any workspace member holding a `write`-scoped key can delete another user's thread or reply. `docs/design/sheets/comments.md:32` states the model as "Comment lifecycle: edit / delete by author only", and the editor enforces exactly that (`packages/frontend/src/components/comments/components/CommentThreadCard.tsx:92`: `c.author.userId === currentUserId`). The new surface therefore permits a destructive action the documented design forbids, and it is irreversible (the thread is removed from the CRDT). Every other comment verb in this controller does resolve the caller (`this.author(req)`), which makes the omission look unintentional rather than a decision recorded anywhere in the diff or in notifications.md.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. `deleteThread` (comments.controller.ts:388-401) and `deleteComment` (:403-431) take only `@Param`s — no `@Req()`, no `this.author(req)`, and no comparison against `comment.author.userId` — while every other mutating verb in the same controller resolves the caller (createThread :247/:255, reply :333/:340, setResolved :364/:371). The documented rule the reviewer cites is real and is a Goal, not a Non-Goal: docs/design/sheets/comments.md:32 and docs/design/docs/docs-comments.md:49 both state "Comment lifecycle: edit / delete by author only", and the editor enforces exactly that at CommentThreadCard.tsx:89-93. No guard makes it unreachable: WorkspaceScopeGuard (workspace-scope.guard.ts:32-46) only checks workspace membership/key binding and ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard (api-key-write-scope.guard.ts:38-49) only checks the `write` scope; neither resolves comment authorship. The originating plan (docs/tasks/active/20260904-class-b-backend-endpoints-todo.md:16, :25-28, :46-60) lists the delete routes in scope and records deliberate divergences for docs-thread creation and tab deletion, but records no decision to drop the author check — so this is an unrecorded contradiction of the canonical design docs, not a documented trade-off. In-lane as spec-conformance/consistency between two surfaces of one feature, and major because the cost lands on users: irreversible deletion of another user's thread from the CRDT by a caller the design forbids.

finding.summary: Notification planning + mention parsing reimplemented in the backend instead of shared, so two copies of the same rule now exist
finding.evidence: `planCommentNotifications`, `toUserId` and `MENTION_RE` in comments.controller.ts are line-for-line restatements of `packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:29-114` and `mentions.ts`' `MENTION_RE`/`extractMentionedUserIds`. The docblock openly says it "applies the same rule the frontend's notify.ts does", and notifications.md (as amended here) promises "membership authorization, the recipient cap and the dedupe keys stay one implementation" — but the *planning* rule (who is a recipient, mention-vs-reply dedupe, actor exclusion) is now two implementations that must be edited in lockstep. The repo's stated posture is reuse via a shared package (`@wafflebase/core`, and the comment engine itself already lives in `@wafflebase/sheets`, from which this controller imports `createThread`/`addReply`/`deleteComment`), so the planning rule and mention regex had an available shared home. Divergence gives two different answers to "who gets notified for this comment" depending on whether the writer was a browser or an agent.

verdict.reason: The duplication is present exactly as described. planCommentNotifications exists in two independent implementations: packages/backend/src/api/v1/comments.controller.ts:532-594 and packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:50-114, with the same three-branch rule (resolve -> participants minus actor; mention set; reply -> earlier participants minus actor minus mentioned). toUserId is byte-for-byte identical (controller:511-515 vs notify.ts:29-33), participantIds duplicates uniqueUserIds (controller:596-603 vs notify.ts:139-146), and MENTION_RE is restated at controller:504 against the canonical mentions.ts:24, with extractMentionedUserIds (mentions.ts:136-144) reimplemented inline at controller:558-564. The controller's own docblock (:88-92) and docs/design/notifications.md:25-31 both state the rule is "the same rule the frontend's notify.ts does" while claiming one implementation only for the service-side cap/dedupe. A shared home was available and already in use: the comment model and thread ops live in @wafflebase/sheets (packages/sheets/src/comment/types.ts:1, index.ts:225,457), which the controller already imports from (:41-46). Divergence is not hypothetical - the frontend flattens mention tokens before preview (notify.ts:35-37,73,92,108) while the backend sends the raw body (controller:550,572,587), so the two planners already produce different payloads for the same comment. This matches the rubric's named major case: duplicated logic that will diverge and give two answers to the same question. Only a minor detail of the reviewer's evidence is imprecise (comment ops are imported from backend-local ../../yorkie/comment-ops, not from @wafflebase/sheets), which does not change the substance.
